texts.preamble: Ankush S/O. Nagnath Patil vs The State Of Maharashtra on 16 January, 2019 Author: Mangesh S. Patil Bench: Mangesh S. Patil 1 31 ba 5.19.o In The High Court Of Judicature At Bombay Bench At Aurangabad Bail Application No.5 Of 2019 Ankush S/O. Nagnath Patil Versus The State Of Maharashtra ... Advocate for Applicant : Mr. Gastgar Santosh B. App for Respondents/State : Mr. S.D. Ghayal ...
texts.facts: Shortly stated the prosecution case is to the effect that several bags of Gutkha were found stocked in the house owned by accused no.2 who happens to be the father in law of the applicant, who is shown as accused no.1. The articles were seized, the matter was reported and the crime was registered. The applicant was arrested on 05.12.2018 and is now seeking bail. The learned advocate for the applicant submits that the applicant no.2 to whom the house belongs from where the Muddemal was seized has been granted bail by the learned Additional Sessions ::: Uploaded on - 17/01/2019 ::: Downloaded on - 18/01/2019 06:52:3 2 31 ba 5.19.odt Judge. The case of the applicant cannot be distinguished rather he stands on a better footing.
texts.arguments: It is under these cirucmstances, presence of the applicant behind the bar is not necessary for completing the investigation. There are no criminal antecedents reported. Even there is a serious doubt about the applicability of Section 328 of the I.P.C. In the facts and circumstances of the case the applicant may be granted bail subject to to usual terms and conditions. 4. The learned A.P.P. opposes the application. He submits that at this juncture the facts cannot be scrutinised to ascertain as to if Section 328 of the I.P.C. is applicable or not. The offence is punishable up to ten years of imprisonment. Gutkha is banned in the State. The applicant was found in possession of a huge stock of Gutkha. The investigation is still in progress and therefore releasing the applicant on bail is likely to hamper the investigation and the application may be rejected. The father in law has been granted bail by the learned Additional Sessions Judge and as has been rightly submitted by the learned advocate the applicant stands on a better footing as compared to his father in law since the house belongs to the father in law.
